clue.text: Title used in all-in wrestling?

parts.note: a legal title to property that is owned outright, read as a grip in no-holds-barred wrestling where any hold is allowed

explanation.surface: A championship belt or wrestler's name used in all-in wrestling bouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a championship or a wrestler's billing, but it is the legal title to land; split the answer in two and it sounds like an unrestricted grip, which suits all-in (anything goes) wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright ownership of land with no time limit is a form of legal title to property.

clue.text: An even chance the matador will try to avoid

definitions.meaning: a situation whose outcome could go either way, like a coin flip

definitions.text: the matador will try to avoid
definitions.meaning: being flung into the air by the bull's horns is what a bullfighter dreads

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: the bull tossing the matador up.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip gives a fifty-fifty chance, so the phrase names any evenly balanced outcome.

clue.text: Pieces played in correct order? Not right

indicators.note: the words are put into a new order, so their letters are rearranged once the letter for right is left out, as Not says

explanation.surface: Asking whether musical pieces were played in the correct sequence, and finding they were not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges IN CORRECT; 'Not right' then takes away one R, leaving eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos are musical works performed by soloist and orchestra, and the Italian plural names several such pieces.

clue.text: Extent of one's education

definitions.meaning: the amount or level to which something happens, as in 'to some extent'
a university qualification earned at the end of a course of study

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a measure of extent and an academic qualification awarded by a university.

clue.text: Exercises with ball in free time

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: in means the ball letter goes inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: Doing exercises with a ball during one's free time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free time' reads as one phrase, but 'free' gives RID and 'time' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time, such as a school lesson or a historical era, is called a period.

clue.text: It holds the shooter's ammunition before shelling starts

definitions.text: It holds the shooter's ammunition before shelling starts

parts.words: It holds the shooter's ammunition before shelling starts
parts.note: the shooter is a child's blowpipe firing dried vegetables, and shelling is removing them from their casing, not a bombardment

explanation.surface: A magazine holding a gunman's ammunition before an artillery bombardment begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture is false: the shooter is a toy that fires small green vegetables, which sit in their casing until someone shells them.
explanation.definitionFit: The seeds fired from a toy shooter grow inside this casing until they are removed for cooking.

clue.text: They are trained to fight dogs

definitions.meaning: fighters in the ring who train for bouts with gloves
a breed of dog with a short muzzle, originally from Germany

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both fighters with gloves in a ring and a German breed of dog.

clue.text: Dry hill region

parts.note: sec is the French word for dry, used of wines
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A dry, hilly area of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or area, so it is a synonym for region.

clue.text: Football club?

parts.note: club read as a body of members, and the formal name of soccer being the game played under the rules of such a body

explanation.walkthrough: Soccer's full name is Association football, after the Football Association; a club is also simply a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a society or body of members, and soccer's formal name comes from such a body.

clue.text: They may be cut or not in the cooking

definitions.text: They may be cut or not in the cooking

parts.words: They may be cut or not in the cooking
parts.note: to cut them is to leap about playfully, while the pickled flower buds go into cooking whole

explanation.surface: Ingredients that may be chopped or left whole when cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests chopping, but 'cut ... ' is an idiom for frisking about; the same word names pickled buds used whole in sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both playful skips (in the idiom of cutting them) and small pickled buds used in cooking.

clue.text: Sporting event in which one has to fire on the run

definitions.text: Sporting event in which one has to fire on the run

parts.words: Sporting event in which one has to fire on the run
parts.note: fire means dismiss, read as the bag the runners stand in, rather than shooting while running

explanation.surface: A shooting competition in which competitors fire while running, like a biathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like shooting; it is the noun for dismissal, the bag that competitors hop along in at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: This school sports-day race has runners hopping inside bags, so it is a sporting event.

clue.text: Very, very fair

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
so again means very

explanation.surface: Something extremely fair or just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' here means mediocre, not just or pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling or only passable, as in a fair performance.

clue.text: One who minds his own business

definitions.text: One who minds his own business

parts.words: One who minds his own business
parts.note: the idiom for not interfering, read literally as looking after a firm one owns

explanation.surface: A discreet person who keeps out of other people's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner who runs a shop or firm is literally looking after a business that is his.

clue.text: I'm unfit and I worry endlessly

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake and tug it about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A person fretting nonstop about being out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means without end, used of something going on forever.

clue.text: Antigone's form of denial

indicators.note: a new form of the name means its letters are reshaped into another word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: How the tragic heroine Antigone expressed her refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigone is the Greek tragic heroine who defied a king's decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of saying no, a contradiction or denial.

clue.text: Girl was about to enter without knowing

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: to enter means the short word for about goes inside the word was

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A girl was about to walk in without anyone knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to enter' reads as 'on the point of entering'; split it, so 'about' is a piece and 'to enter' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken unawares means caught by surprise, without knowing what was coming.

clue.text: Packed for daughter going to public school

indicators.note: the daughter's letter goes to the school, attaching at its end

parts.note: Stowe is an English public (private fee-paying) school in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: Bags packed for a daughter heading off to boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an expensive private school; Stowe is a well-known one.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away, so the past tense means packed.

clue.text: Customer's right established in court

indicators.note: established in means the word for a right is set inside the short form of court

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A customer's legal right being confirmed by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a person who buys services from a professional, a customer.

clue.text: On the level? Yes and no

definitions.text: On the level? Yes and no

parts.words: On the level? Yes and no
parts.note: the phrase means honest, but its first word means level while its second means the opposite

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is honest, someone gives an equivocal answer.
explanation.walkthrough: On the level means honest, which fits the whole phrase; but its first half is flat and level and its second half points skywards, hence yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: Being honest and truthful is what the idiom means, the same as being on the level.

clue.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

definitions.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

parts.words: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?
parts.note: an early (morning) bird sitting in a shrub to pounce, read as a trap laid for a victim

explanation.surface: Where a bird that rises early waits for its worm.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap for an enemy is pictured as a bird hiding in foliage; 'early' also gives AM, the morning, before the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise attack from a hiding place is exactly what a lurking bird waiting for a worm carries out.

clue.text: Creature that can't fly and another one that can

definitions.text: Creature that can't fly and another one that can

parts.words: Creature that can't fly and another one that can
parts.note: the farm animal from 'pigs might fly', followed by enough letters to make a bird that does fly

explanation.surface: Contrasting a flightless creature with one that flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature that can't fly' points to an ostrich or penguin, but it is the farm animal of 'pigs might fly', which starts this flying bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This common town bird is a creature that can fly, and it begins with a farmyard animal that cannot.

clue.text: Turning point in tax legislation

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words tax legislation

explanation.surface: A turning point in the history of tax law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning point' looks like a decisive moment; it is literally a rod a wheel turns on.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns about this rod, so it is the point of turning.

clue.text: How crocodiles travel?

parts.note: crocodiles are lines of schoolchildren walking in pairs, not reptiles

explanation.surface: A question about how the reptiles get about.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs; the phrase also recalls animals entering Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A school crocodile walks in pairs, which is the manner the phrase describes.

clue.text: Wine vaults?

definitions.meaning: a red or white wine from the Bordeaux region of France
burial places, such as tombs in a churchyard

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Bordeaux wine and burial places, which are sometimes vaults.

clue.text: He has absolute control of the French vessel

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.surface: A man who rules over the French ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant or autocrat holds absolute power over a state or people.

clue.text: Diffident in two ways

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
ST, street, is a way in the sense of a road

explanation.surface: Being shy in two different respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in two ways' looks like a comment on the definition but gives two words for way.
explanation.definitionFit: A diffident person is shy and unassuming, which is a synonym for modest.
